title: Letter from Visa regarding service disruption, 15 June 2018
institution: Visa Europe (Charlotte Hogg); published by the UK Parliament Treasury Committee
location: Printed pp. 1–5; hardware sequence p. 2; transaction attempts p. 4
kind: Primary source — company incident account submitted to Parliament
scope_en: Visa's European processing systems during the incident; transaction attempts, not unique people.
support_en: Visa reported 5.2 million unsuccessful processing attempts out of 51.2 million submissions, approximately 10%; accounting for retries roughly halved the failure measure. It described a partial switch failure that disrupted failover and stated the incident was not cyber-related.
limits_en: Contemporaneous company account, not the final independent root-cause review; failures are not necessarily lost purchases. Retain the source's rounded 10%.

title: Bank of England announces supervisory action over Visa Europe’s June 2018 partial outage incident
location: News release, paragraphs 1–8
scope_en: Visa Europe's card authorization system; UK supervision of the European incident.
support_en: Following an independent review, the Bank directed Visa Europe to implement the recommendations and required PwC to assess progress. It identified widespread disruption and possible damage to confidence in the financial system.
limits_en: The Bank expressly said this was not enforcement action and did not imply a regulatory breach; it was not a fine.

title: Visa Inc. Facts & Figures, November 2015
location: P. 1, Our History and Key Facts
kind: Primary source — corporate historical fact sheet
scope_en: Visa's origin, brand formation, restructuring and initial public offering.
support_en: BankAmericard launched in 1958; the Visa brand formed in 1976 and Visa Inc. was created through restructuring in 2007. The fact sheet dates Visa's IPO to 2008-03-19.
limits_en: Historical source only; its 2015 financial, leadership and scale information is not current evidence. It does not establish a world-first claim.

title: Brand History
location: Building a Global Brand; Brand Mark Evolution
scope_en: Mastercard's association origins, rule setting, brand and ownership changes.
support_en: The Interbank Card Association originated in 1966, with committees establishing authorization, clearing and settlement rules; Master Charge became MasterCard in 1979. The Europay merger and conversion to a private share corporation occurred in 2002, followed by an IPO in 2006.
limits_en: Publication date is undisclosed; distinguish 1966 origins from the page's 1967 formal charter. Undated marketing statistics are excluded.

title: Electronic Point-of-Sale Payments
location: Development of bank-issued credit cards; Early 1970s proposals; development of private networks
kind: Institutional historical synthesis — based on earlier records
scope_en: US bank-card development and the Federal Reserve's infrastructure choices.
support_en: Expansion beyond individual banks created interbank-settlement needs, initially served through paper records and telephone authorization. The Fed considered point-of-sale switching but left its development to private actors following the 1977 commission recommendation.
limits_en: Institutional synthesis, not contemporaneous primary evidence for every event; it does not establish a global chronology or privatization of all payment infrastructure.

title: Overview of EMVCo
location: FAQs: Who is EMVCo?; How does EMVCo operate?; specifications mandate question
scope_en: Global payment interoperability specifications and testing governance.
support_en: EMVCo formed in 1999 to manage interoperable secure-payment specifications and testing. Its six owners are American Express, Discover, JCB, Mastercard, UnionPay and Visa; EMVCo states that it does not mandate use of its specifications.
limits_en: Undated page; access date is not publication date. Standard setting does not make EMVCo a settlement network, regulator or guarantee against all fraud.

title: MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme and processing fees: final report
event_or_period: 2017–2023 fee analysis; detailed incremental-cost baselines: Mastercard 2017, Visa 2018
scope_en: UK acquiring-side core scheme and processing fees; real growth; monetary amounts in GBP.
support_en: PSR found core fees relative to transaction value rose at least 25% in real terms over 2017–2023, implying at least GBP 170 million additional annual cost. It distinguishes issuer interchange, network charges and acquirer revenue, and describes card-linked wallets as interfaces.
limits_en: UK findings, not global prices or adjudicated damages; reliable UK cost data were insufficient. Redactions remain unknown; reproduced UK Finance/BRC estimates retain their third-party status.

title: PS26/1: Market review of card scheme and processing fees: Final decision — Information, transparency and complexity remedy; pricing governance remedy
event_or_period: Final directions 2026-07-30; pricing governance from end-November 2026; substantive information requirements from end-July 2027
location: Policy statement webpage, opening paragraphs and implementation dates
kind: Primary source — final regulatory policy decision
scope_en: UK Mastercard and Visa scheme/processing fee transparency and pricing governance.
support_en: Two final directions require clearer fee/reconciliation information and better evidence for pricing decisions. Relevant pricing decisions must comply from end-November 2026, and substantive information requirements apply from end-July 2027.
limits_en: These compliance dates remain future at the 2026-10-08 cutoff. This is not a price cap or evidence of realized fee reductions; financial reporting was a separate measure.

title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
location: Press release, opening paragraphs and conduct allegations
kind: Primary source — plaintiff's announcement of allegations
scope_en: Alleged conduct in US debit-network markets.
support_en: DOJ filed a civil antitrust suit alleging that Visa used exclusionary contracts and agreements with potential competitors to protect its debit-network position.
limits_en: Allegations are not liability findings. Litigation market-share claims are excluded from the industry chart, and this announcement does not establish subsequent case status.

title: Memorandum Opinion and Order, United States v. Visa Inc., 24-cv-7214 (JGK), Document 89
institution: US District Court, Southern District of New York; Judge John G. Koeltl; hosted by DOJ
location: Pp. 1–3 and 58
kind: Primary source — court order at the pleadings stage
scope_en: Procedural ruling on Visa's motion to dismiss the US antitrust complaint.
support_en: The court denied Visa's motion to dismiss and explained that complaint facts were accepted as true for that motion. Visa disputed market definition, the pricing allegations and the interpretation of its agreements.
limits_en: Not a trial judgment or finding of liability; the order does not prove that no later procedural developments occurred.

title: Joint EBA-ECB report on payment fraud: strong authentication remains effective but fraudsters are adapting
institution: European Banking Authority and European Central Bank
location: Headline bullets and paragraphs 1–7
kind: Primary source — joint regulatory statistical release
scope_en: EEA payment fraud; card-loss subset covers EU/EEA-issued cards; EUR.
support_en: Reported payment fraud reached EUR 4.2 billion in 2024; card losses for EU/EEA-issued cards were EUR 1.329 billion. Strong authentication generally reduced card fraud, while exploitation of exemptions and manipulation of legitimate payers remained concerns.
limits_en: EUR 4.2 billion is not card-only fraud or a global figure. Transfer fraud is not exclusively instant-payment fraud; network operators do not necessarily bear all reported losses.

title: Fees for card-based payments — Summary of Regulation (EU) 2015/751
institution: Publications Office of the European Union / EUR-Lex
location: Key points; Main document
scope_en: Covered consumer card interchange in the EU, subject to exemptions and national options.
support_en: Covered consumer debit interchange is capped at 0.2% and consumer credit interchange at 0.3%, with exemptions including qualifying commercial cards. These limits concern interchange rather than total merchant charges or network revenue.
limits_en: The official summary was read; the full-law link redirected during this session. Do not infer the cap commencement date or universal coverage of international/commercial transactions.

title: Innovations in payments
institution: Morten Bech and Jenny Hancock; BIS Quarterly Review
location: Payments: a primer; PDF edition begins at printed p. 21
scope_en: Global payment terminology and settlement design.
support_en: Clearing exchanges and reconciles instructions; settlement transfers funds to discharge obligations, with finality identifying an irrevocable and unconditional transfer. Net settlement economizes on liquidity while leaving exposure until settlement; real-time gross settlement needs more funding.
limits_en: Use the conceptual definitions, not outdated statistics or service-launch forecasts. It does not imply all retail payments settle directly at a central bank.

title: Fast payments: design and adoption
location: Key takeaways; Infrastructure; Cross-country analysis
kind: Institutional research — cross-country analysis; authors' views
scope_en: Fast-payment system design and adoption across 13 jurisdictions.
support_en: Adoption was associated with public ownership, nonbank participation, more use cases and cross-border connections. Immediate availability to users can coexist with either real-time or deferred inter-provider settlement.
limits_en: Association is not universal causal proof; authors' views are not necessarily BIS/CPMI policy. Selected-jurisdiction data do not constitute global payment-market shares.

title: Council adopts regulation on instant payments
location: Press release, paragraphs 1–7
scope_en: Euro instant credit transfers within the regulation's EU/EEA scope.
support_en: Covered providers must offer instant euro transfers after transition periods, with ten-second availability around the clock and charges no higher than corresponding ordinary transfers. Beneficiary verification and access provisions accompany the speed requirement.
limits_en: The adoption release does not prove universal compliance by 2026-10-08 or supply every implementation deadline. It does not make all instant payments free or replicate card protections automatically.

title: Global Brand Cards Worldwide — Midyear 2024, Nilson Report Issue 1276
location: pp. 16–17, Global Brand General Purpose Cards table and adjacent text
kind: Original industry research; third-party measurement; JCB estimated
scope_en: Worldwide purchases on six global card brands; consumer, small-business and commercial credit, debit and prepaid cards; USD value excludes cash advances/withdrawals.
support_en: H 1 2024 purchase value $17,365.17 bn: Visa 37.42%, UnionPay 33.90%, Mastercard 22.15%, Amex 4.91%, JCB 0.91%, Discover/Diners 0.71%. Shares sum 100.00%; Visa+Mastercard 59.57%. Purchase transactions 363.93 bn. Publisher PDF text and rendered pp 16–17 verified.
limits_en: Historical six-brand universe, not all payments or all infrastructure. Mastercard excludes Maestro/Cirrus. JCB estimated. Source shares used unchanged; no normalization. Newer complete six-brand data not accessible. Source PDF retained for inspection only; distribute link, not original.

title: Global Network Card Results Worldwide — 2025, Issue 1310
location: Public opening paragraph; publication date on nilsonreport.com/newsletters/1310/
kind: Original industry research, publicly readable excerpt
scope_en: Worldwide goods/services purchase transactions on Visa, UnionPay, Mastercard, Amex, JCB and Discover/Diners; consumer/small-business/commercial; debit includes prepaid.
support_en: 2025 transactions 828.10 bn, up 7.1% year on year. Newer scale observation can accompany separately dated H 1 2024 share chart.
limits_en: Full brand breakdown subscription-only; public chart numerals blurred. No exact 2025 brand shares used, and no splice with H 1 2024 chart.

title: Visa Reports Fiscal Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2025 Results
location: Full-year highlights p3; financial summary p6; consolidated operations p8
scope_en: Visa worldwide consolidated fiscal results, USD; GAAP unless stated.
support_en: Revenue $40.000 bn (+11%); operating income $23.994 bn; net income $20.058 bn. Calculated operating margin 23.994/40.000=60.0% rounded. Client incentives $15.751 bn deducted from gross revenue categories. Processed transactions 257.5 bn.
limits_en: Fiscal year ends September, not Mastercard's December. Processing count is not all Visa-branded purchase count. Company revenue is not payment value or industry market share. GAAP includes litigation/severance effects.

title: Mastercard Incorporated 2025 Form 10-K
location: pp6–7,49–56,68; Note3 Revenue pp82–83
kind: Company annual report / primary financial disclosure
scope_en: Worldwide consolidated calendar-year GAAP financial results and defined operating drivers.
support_en: Supports the annual financial table, services revenue, gross-dollar-volume definition and remaining service obligations. Calculations and units appear once in the calculation record.
limits_en: Fiscal dates differ from Visa. Cash is included in GDV. Services revenue is not standalone profit; service obligations are not total company backlog.

title: Visa Reports Fiscal Third Quarter 2026 Results
location: Financial highlights p2, financial summary p5, consolidated operations p7
scope_en: Worldwide consolidated GAAP quarterly results; Visa FY 2026 Q 3.
support_en: Revenue $11.633 bn (+14%; constant-dollar+13%); operating income $6.877 bn; net income $5.628 bn. Calculated margin 6.877/11.633=59.1%. Processed transactions 71.7 bn (+10%). Payments growth 10% constant dollar; client incentives $4.680 bn (+18%).
limits_en: Quarter matches M 06 despite fiscal name. Service revenue uses prior-quarter payments volume. Brand volume versus processed count differ. Visa ex-Europe cross-border growth should not be compared with Mastercard total without scope caveat.

title: Mastercard Incorporated Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
location: Quarterly operating results p1, business drivers p2, consolidated operations p7
scope_en: Worldwide consolidated GAAP calendar Q 2 2026 results.
support_en: Revenue $9.277 bn (+14%; currency-neutral+12%); operating income $5.587 bn; margin 60.2%; net income $4.388 bn. Purchase value+10% local currency; switched transactions+9%. Services revenue+20%; network revenue+10%; network rebates/incentives+22% reported.
limits_en: Use this calendar quarter to match M 05. Consolidated company revenue is not a market-share denominator. Local/currency-neutral definitions and processing measures remain company-specific; no 2026 annual extrapolation.

title: Payments lifecycle and Global acquiring
location: Authorization statuses; Capture and settlement statuses; Global acquiring overview
scope_en: Adyen services; illustrative of card payment operations, not a universal rulebook.
support_en: Authorization reserves funds. A settled status at Adyen does not necessarily mean the merchant has been paid. Adyen provides processing and acquiring.
limits_en: No publication date is displayed. No provider performance, market share or universal payout schedule is inferred.

title: EMV Payment Tokenisation
published: Undated overview; listed framework v2.4 publication 2026-07-09
location: What is EMV Payment Tokenisation; Specifications; FAQs
scope_en: EMV payment tokens in card payments worldwide.
support_en: A payment token substitutes for the primary account number and can be restricted to a merchant, device or use case while using existing payment infrastructure.
limits_en: Not a blockchain token or settlement asset. This explanation is not a measured guarantee of fraud prevention. The complete v 2.4 specification was not audited.

title: Visa Launches Stablecoin Settlement in the United States
location: Opening paragraphs; Expanding a proven foundation; FAQ; footnote 1
scope_en: Selected US institutions settling Visa obligations in USDC; run rate relates to Visa stablecoin settlement activity.
support_en: Cross River Bank and Lead Bank began USDC settlement over Solana. Visa reported a monthly-volume annualized run rate above USD 3.5 bn, not realized full-year volume.
limits_en: Broader 2026 availability was a plan in this release. It does not prove all Visa transactions settle onchain or that bank and issuer risks disappear.

title: Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
location: Principles 8 and 9
scope_en: Relevant financial market infrastructures; general analytical benchmark, not a claim of identical legal applicability to every provider.
support_en: Rules should define settlement finality. Settlement in commercial bank money requires control of credit and liquidity risk; central bank money is preferred where practical and available.
limits_en: A successful authorization or blockchain confirmation alone is not a legal determination of finality. No provider compliance certification is asserted.
